passage: L1.3: "Feature selection on the entire dataset results in using information about which feature performs well" (Results, 'Toward a solution: A taxonomy of data leakage', PMC10499856; the sentence is cut by the fetch tool). The reference list also cites a paper on inflated accuracy from feature selection in neuropsychiatric biomarkers (ref. 34), not described in the text.
faulty: The 20 features with the largest absolute two-sample t statistic between y True and y False are chosen on all 80 rows; then 5-fold cross-validation (stratified: fold = rank of the row within its class mod 5) of a ridge classifier (ridge regression on y coded +1/-1, lambda 10, standardised, on the 20 chosen features); pooled AUC over all 80 held-out scores >= 0.65.
fixed: In each fold the 20 features are chosen from the 64 training rows only, the ridge classifier is fitted on them, scores the 16 held-out rows; pooled AUC >= 0.65.
estimand: Faulty: AUC of a classifier whose features were chosen with the held-out labels. Fixed: the out-of-sample AUC of the whole pipeline (feature choice plus classifier) for new subjects.
model_family: Top-20 filter by absolute t statistic, then ridge classifier (ridge regression on +/-1 labels, lambda 10, standardised). Source names none; numpy-only and defined with 1000 features on 80 rows.
sizes_note: Source states none. 80 x 1000 = 80,000 values: small-n many-features regime typical of biomarker studies; the check is 5 t-test sweeps and 5 small ridge fits (seconds). Dependence of the error on number of features: not stated (the source only says selection on the entire dataset uses information about which feature performs well on the test set).
exploited_structure: Many candidate features relative to the number of samples, so the features with the largest apparent association with the labels include chance associations that the held-out rows also carry.
